messages:
jia: Heads up — on iPhone SE (320px) the Invocations table is overflowing horizontally and the left-edge swipe to open the nav steals the horizontal scroll. Screenshot attached. repro: Console > Recent invocations, try a quick horizontal swipe on a row. Repro rate ~80%

sam: ugh. can you paste the CSS/layout tree? is the table inside a scrollable container or using display:flex/grid?

jia: it's a simple grid inside .console-main. .invocations-table currently has overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; but our edge-swipe gesture listens on the outer container so the nav opens instead of letting the inner scroll take the gesture.

mateo: could we debounce or lower the edge-swipe priority? on iOS the system edge-swipe is hard to intercept but our JS layer definitely competes.

olivia: also an a11y concern — keyboard focus sometimes jumps to the nav when tabbing near the left edge. we should ensure focus doesn't accidentally move and that screen readers get a clear announcement when nav opens.

jia: quick proposals: 1) for widths <=360px switch to a bottom sheet for details (no right rail), 2) collapse row actions into a kebab menu to reduce horizontal width, 3) fallback: treat rows as stacked cards at tiny widths.

sam: bottom sheet and stacked cards are two different UXs. bottom-sheet is less disruptive to learn. stacked cards change density a lot. personally leaning bottom-sheet as minimum churn.

mateo: quick CSS mitigation we can try immediately: set touch-action: pan-x on the inner scroll container so horizontal pan gestures are honored, and make the rail edge gesture require a wider deliberate swipe (increase threshold). CSS:```css
.invocations-scroll { overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; touch-action: pan-x; }
```

olivia: plus a copy/accessibility tweak: truncate long model names with ellipsis and expose full name via title and aria-label. ensure row has role=row and the primary cell has tabindex=0 so keyboard users can get into the row without accidentally triggering nav.

jia: i'll prototype bottom-sheet + kebab actions and include the CSS touch-action quick fix in a deploy preview. if both exist we can A/B them.

prod-bot: deploy-preview created: https://deployments.redwood/preview/1829004731 — includes touch-action change and provisional bottom-sheet mock. logs: build success.

sam: tested preview on iPhone SE simulator. touch-action helps for slow swipes but very fast edge swipes still open nav. bottom-sheet completely avoids the conflict — looks good.

mateo: +1 bottom-sheet. also enforce 44px minimum target for any row action buttons. small buttons are killing tap accuracy.

olivia: tiny copy nit while we're here: in the details header change "Invocation" to "Request" to match the product naming guidelines. also add an accessible close button label: aria-label="Close request details".

jia: noted and updating mocks. i'll add an accessibility checklist to the PR: focus order, aria roles, 44px hit targets, keyboard open/close behavior, announcements.

sam: sounds good. quick plan: ship touch-action hotfix to prod today, land bottom-sheet + kebab actions in the next sprint, run 10% A/B traffic to measure drop-off in accidental nav opens and interaction success. :thumbsup:

jia: thanks all — i'll post the mock links and the PR once ready.
